Check whether Jessica Jones is payable (3 energy) — her 2 ATK is our second damage source. If no energy is available, I'll cancel and just attack.

Keep Strength and Helicarrier intact for now (the horn's +1 ATK is manageable since DEF 3 covers it) and end the turn to draw a fresh hand of 6 cards, including hopefully energy resources.

Haymaker (3) plus Black Cat's attack (1) will finish it this turn, before the villain phase where Rhino and Vulture would both attack (3+5 damage). Killing Vulture also cuts a point of threat per round.
Pay Haymaker's 2-cost with the Energy card (2 energy), keeping Mockingbird, Black Cat and Heroic Intuition for the Black Cat play that follows.
Play Black Cat (paying with Mockingbird + Heroic Intuition) so she can attack Vulture for 1 damage, finishing it off this turn before it can hit us for 5 next round.
Finish Vulture with Black Cat's 1 damage — it is the 5-ATK villainous nemesis and removing it also stops 1 threat per round. Killing it now avoids taking 5 damage in the villain phase.

Stay in hero form (hero form keeps the villain from scheming, so threat only grows 2/round instead of 3/round) and end the turn with an empty hand to draw 5 fresh cards for round 3, when I need both 4 damage on Rhino and threat removal.

(4 if paid with a mental resource) plus 1 with the hero's THW, which covers the 2/round accrual comfortably. Keeping the free interrupt for a critical moment later is better than spending 2 HP now.

I keep the hero ready for round 3 (hero ATK 2) and I have Backflip in hand as a free interrupt that can prevent all of Rhino's attack damage if the engine offers a damage window. Defending with the hero would exhaust it and defending with Black Cat (2 HP) would likely kill her, so taking 2 now is the best option.

Backflip is free and prevents all 3 damage without exhausting Spider-Man (unlike defending, which would cost my ATK/THW next turn). I want to stay at 8 HP and keep the hero ready for round 3's damage push.

Defeating Highway Robbery removes the acceleration (threat accrual drops from 2/round to 1/round) and returns Nick Fury to my hand, whose 4-damage entry can then kill Rhino. Paying with two non-mental cards (Aunt May + Spider-Tracer) keeps the 4-removal mental option (Great Responsibility) in reserve.

Pay For Justice! with Aunt May + Spider-Tracer (2 energy, no mental) for 3 threat, which exactly defeats Highway Robbery, and keep Webbed Up (4 physical) to pay for Nick Fury and Great Responsibility in hand for a future 4-removal.
Rhino has a tough status, so this 1-damage hit is fully prevented and the tough is consumed — setting up Nick Fury's 4 damage to land in full and kill Rhino this turn.

Black Cat is exhausted and I have no payable cards, so the hero's 2 ATK is my only damage source this turn. Bringing Rhino to 2 HP sets up a kill next round (or with a big card draw), and the acceleration on Highway Robbery is gone so threat only grows 1/round.
No further legal actions (no payable cards, Black Cat exhausted). End the turn to draw 2 more cards — I need damage cards and physical resources to keep pace with 31 remaining villain hit points.
Keep all three cards (Webbed Up to stun a villain attack, Great Responsibility to convert threat into damage, Nick Fury for 4 damage or 2 THW) and draw up to 5.

Holding Great Responsibility is better: used at a later window it prevents the same 1 threat while saving us 1 HP, and it keeps the option open in case other threat removal (For Justice!, Nick Fury's 2 THW) is needed earlier. Threat 4/7 is still safe this round.

Defending with Black Cat (2 HP) soaks Rhino's 2-3 damage at the cost of only 0-1 excess damage to me, while keeping Spider-Man ready — the hero's 2 ATK and 1 THW are our most valuable free resources for the grind against 31 remaining villain HP.

Plan for round 4: play Jessica Jones (2 ATK, and THW 1+1 per side scheme, which becomes 2 once Breakin' & Takin' appears) to kill stage 1 with her 2 ATK, then use the hero's 2 ATK on stage 2, and bring in Nick Fury (4 damage + 2 ATK). All three of my small cards (First Aid, Great Responsibility, Interrogation Room) plus Webbed Up are the only resources available, so I'll spend them to fuel both allies.
Pay Jessica Jones with Great Responsibility + First Aid + Interrogation Room (3 resources), keeping Webbed Up (4) in hand so I can still pay for Nick Fury's 4 cost in the same turn.

Jessica Jones's 2 ATK finishes stage 1 exactly (Rhino has 2 HP), so no damage is wasted and stage 2 appears immediately — after which the hero's 2 ATK and Nick Fury's 4+2 can all hit the 15-HP stage 2.
With stage 1 dead, the hero's 2 ATK goes to the fresh 15-HP stage 2, and I keep the option of playing Nick Fury (4) afterwards if the engine allows it.
No further legal plays (the hero is exhausted and no card is payable), and I want to stay in hero form to avoid the villain's scheme boost adding threat. Ending the turn to draw 3 fresh cards.
Hand is only 2 cards, well under the hand size of 5, so no discards — I keep Webbed Up (stall) and Nick Fury (4 damage) and draw 3 more cards.

Jessica Jones is worth far more than 2 HP: her 2 ATK plus THW 2 (one side scheme is in play) is our main damage and threat-removal engine with 30 villain HP still to chew through. Defending with the hero would also cost me next round's basic power, and defending with JJ kills her outright. So I take the hit and keep her alive.

Enhanced Spider-Sense cancels the treachery's When Revealed effect, preventing my identity from being stunned — a stun would waste my next attack, which is critical with only 4 HP left and 30 villain HP to go.

Pay the 1-cost with Interrogation Room (1 energy, exact match). It only helps after a minion is defeated and we have no minions, whereas I want to keep The Power of Justice (2 wild), Nick Fury and Webbed Up for the damage and stall plays ahead.
